messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — AureliaBridge onboarding looks healthy on feature adoption, but we're seeing rising token spend and p95 latency during peak windows. Renewal in ~30d. I want to propose a proactive performance play: run an INT8 quantization pilot + model swap to redwood-compat-v2.1 for short-chat traffic, and add a routing policy that prefers the quantized variant with an automatic fallback to the fp16 model on quality or latency regressions. Asking eng + SRE to scope a canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%), warm-up plan, and a one-pager for the customer. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Priya: Sharing quick stats from the last 48h: p50 ~120ms, p95 jumped 430ms -> 620ms during two spikes, token cost up ~22% month-over-month. Traffic mix: ~70% short-turn chat (<64 tokens), ~30% long context. INT8 looks promising for the short-turn bulk. Recommend: INT8 for <128 tokens, keep mixed-precision for >128, and monitor QA metrics (BLEU/QA-specific metrics we use). I'll attach sample traces after this thread. :bar_chart:

Ethan: Agree with targeted quantization. Two engineering caveats: (1) model-swap may introduce small output distribution changes — we need to run the customer's eval suite (we have their compliance prompts) before moving >25%. (2) routing fallback should be latency+quality aware. I can set up the canary pipeline and quality checks. Proposed rollout plan: canary 5% (48h), expand to 25% if eval metrics within delta, then 100% after 7 days of stability. Also add automatic rollback on quality delta > 1.5% or latency > 2x baseline. :white_check_mark:

Diego: Infra notes: Dedicated pool utilization is fine but cache-warm will be required for a quantized model to hit steady latencies. Plan: seed top 500 prefixes and ramp traffic over 6 hours during low-traffic window. Also watch KV cache hit rate and GPU memory footprint (INT8 changes memory layout). If we warm without ramping, we'll see an artificial latency spike and CS will panic. I'll coordinate a 2-hour maintenance window if needed. :warning:

Maya: Thanks — @Ethan can you prepare the eval harness and quick quality dashboard? @Diego confirm if we need a maintenance window and recommended time (low-traffic). I'll start drafting the customer note and enablement playbook with rollback steps and expected benefits (latency down, cost -18% estimated).

Ethan: Will do. Quick config snippet for routing I can push to the canary repo — this is the basic rule we'll use:

```
route_rules:
  - match: "request.tokens <= 128"
    prefer: "aurelia-int8-v2.1"
    fallback: "aurelia-fp16-v2.1"
    fallback_condition:
      - type: "latency"
        threshold_ms: 800
      - type: "quality"
        delta_allowed: 0.015
  - match: "request.tokens > 128"
    prefer: "aurelia-fp16-v2.1"
```

Ethan: Canary will include automatic sampling of 1% of requests to store full responses for QA. We'll run diff-based quality checks on those samples.

Priya: I'll prepare the CS-facing one-pager: expected p95 reduction, estimated cost savings, rollback steps, and suggested customer talking points. Also capturing feedback loop: daily quality summary for first 7 days, then weekly.

Diego: Confirmed — we can do a warm-up during Sat 02:00-04:00 UTC. I recommend the 6-hour ramp starting at 02:00. I'll reserve cap and post the maintenance note. Also: remember to seed KV prefixes before traffic ramp.

Maya: Perfect. I'll send the customer note after we have the eval harness link and the one-pager. Renewal team: flagging this as a proactive engagement to reduce renewal risk — target: demonstrate stable p95 and cost savings within 2 weeks of canary. :rocket: 

ai-deploy-bot: Canary pipeline scheduled (tentative): 1765060000. Notifying #eng-releases and #eng-oncall automatically.

Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the calendar invites and the draft note. :thumbsup:
